extracted.intended_audience: corporate finance, sustainability and reporting teams preparing TCFD/ISSB/IFRS S1-S2 climate-related financial disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Practical considerations and guidance for preparing climate-related financial disclosures aligned to the TCFD framework (and incorporated into ISSB/IFRS S1 and S2). Aimed at entities planning or advancing their climate-related reporting across governance, strategy, risk management, metrics and targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: The reporting journey
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related financial disclosures should be viewed as a journey rather than a destination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because climate change is dynamic and developing, ongoing evaluations are necessary to account for changing progression and updated impacts from scientific data and analysis. Transparency about where an entity is in its reporting journey helps users understand progress. Example: Smiths Group FY2023 report stating FY2024 priorities and plans to continue aligning with recommendations and conduct quantitative scenario analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on what is material
rubrics_metrics.description: The length and content of disclosures should be driven by information that is material to an understanding of an entity's development, performance and position regarding climate-related financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key messages should not be obscured by volume. Use links to existing information in the annual report rather than duplicating disclosures. Consider materiality tests to decide what to include. Empirical context: FCA study showed regulated companies averaged 15 pages of disclosures and non-regulated companies averaged 5 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time horizons
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification for chosen time horizons should be linked to the overall business strategy and not solely to addressing climate risks/opportunities; climate-related timeframes are often much longer than traditional financial timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing time horizons consider factors such as the life of assets, budgetary cycles, length of financing arrangements, the profile of climate-related risks faced, sectors and geographies of operation, and the nature of the company’s business and operations. Explain why selected horizons are appropriate relative to strategy and climate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking to the overall risk management process
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities must disclose how processes for identifying, assessing and managing climate-related risks are integrated into their overall risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should be a clear connection between disclosures on managing climate-related risks/opportunities and the entity’s broader risk management framework for other principal risks and opportunities. Provide concrete integration examples. Example referenced: DiscoverIE Group plc Annual Report (page 45).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of data on a timely basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Set targets with a clear baseline period and ensure access to data and a consistent methodology to monitor progress and achievability of targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely setting targets is insufficient — entities must be able to monitor performance against a defined baseline and apply consistent methods so management can judge achievability. Ensure data availability and timeliness for tracking progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events after the reporting period
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures should align with the reporting period of the annual report and focus on the entity's state during that period, while also being helpful about future changes (planned or executed) given the evolving regulatory environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat climate-related events after the reporting period similarly to post balance sheet events: consider a separate note or a summary at the end of the relevant section to distinguish period-related activities from future activities. This ensures clarity between activities relating to the reported period and those relating to future periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics and targets
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a clear linkage between principal climate-related risks and opportunities disclosed and the corresponding metrics and targets (GHG metrics are widely used due to the GHG Protocol).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select metrics and targets that are relevant to identified risks and opportunities so reporting is cohesive and demonstrates relevance to users. Use tables to show linkage between metrics/targets and TCFD recommendations or identified risks. Example: Smiths Group FY2023 report showing relationship between metrics and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope 3 captures all emissions an entity is indirectly responsible for through its value chain (upstream and downstream) across 15 reporting categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities should disclose all applicable Scope 3 categories and provide details of which categories were included in their disclosed Scope 3 emissions. This supports comparability to peers, transparency of metrics, and links to targets/performance. Use the 15-category framework to measure, manage and reduce value-chain emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid providing general, broad information on climate change in disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures should clearly explain the precise effects of climate-related risks and opportunities as they apply to the entity’s business model and processes — not broad statements. Be specific about impacts, pathways, and implications for the entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure transparency and connectivity between narrative reporting and climate-related assumptions and estimates; users demand better linkage to assess resilience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit the judgements, estimates and assumptions used when evaluating the impact of climate-related risks and opportunities. Connect narrative sections to the climate-related assumptions and estimates in financial and non-financial reporting so users can assess and compare entity resilience to climate change.
